title: Johan C NDE 4945
content: I was in a very weak state later described by the medical staff in layman's terms of a 'walking coma'. Except for this event, I have little recall of a four to five month time period. I was watching TV and the room/world went silent and dark with my eyes wide open. Time ceased. No pain at all or sense of environment. Except for my mind's eye, all senses were gone. It was very black and not the least bit frightening, a very calm transition. I knew what was happening and it was fine. I honestly wanted to see where this journey led me. If one can imagine oneself in the absolute void of space this was it. Then I saw the twinkling of lights. I sensed from deep within something like 'Are you sure?' With that conscious thought, I decided I wanted to live and the battle was on. Death did not wish to let me go and that's when the experience devolved. I can only describe the experience as what someone might have on a bad acid trip. The next moment, a team of doctors and nurses back here attended to me. I had not moved. I wrote the experience off as a bad dream or a nightmare. After speaking with the psychologist at the hospital several things were pointed out to me including the fact I dream in black and white and this event was in Technicolor. I now have absolutely no fear of death only the pain associated with it.

tunnel.passage_other_detail: Absolute void of space; everything went silent and dark with eyes open; all senses gone except 'mind's eye'.

boundary_and_return.return_reason_other_detail: He consciously decided he wanted to live after sensing 'Are you sure?'

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Very weak state described by medical staff as a 'walking coma'.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Transition into a silent dark void; later 'devolved' into an experience described like a bad acid trip; then medical staff attended to him.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Silent/dark void with timelessness; twinkling lights; internal sensed question ('Are you sure?'); chose to live; distressing phase; then back with doctors and nurses.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: He described the later phase as like a 'bad acid trip' and framed the initial phase as a calm 'walking coma' transition into an absolute void of space.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “Time ceased.” “If one can imagine oneself in the absolute void of space this was it.” “I sensed from deep within something like ‘Are you sure?’” “I now have absolutely no fear of death only the pain associated with it.”
